sentences.text: The only known specimen of Mopsitta tanta is a single humerus bone of large size.
The species is nicknamed the "Danish Blue Parrot" or "Norwegian Blue" after a Monty Python sketch.
Mopsitta tanta is an extinct bird found in the Early Eocene of Denmark, with remains recovered from the Fur Formation.
Mopsitta is classified within the parent group Psittaciformes.
Researchers initially thought Mopsitta tanta might be the oldest known crown-group parrot because it resembled Recent Psittacidae.
Mopsitta lived during the Ypresian stage, between 56 and 48.07 million years ago.

Further examination revealed that the fossil lacks clear features defining it as a psittaciform or psittacid. It is debated whether the humerus belongs to Mopsitta tanta or the ibis genus Rhynchaeites, as it matches Rhynchaeites better except for size.
